card.tagline: Spain, 15th century — Ute ceremonial dance that occurs in the spring
card.profile: Bear Dance is a Ute ceremonial dance that occurs in the spring. It is a ten-day event to strengthen social ties within the community, encourage courtship, and mark the end of puberty for girls. The event includes dancing, feasting, games, horse racing, and gambling. It is one of the oldest Ute ceremonies. The Bear Dance was first recorded by Spanish conquistadors in the 15th century, but oral tradition dates it to be a thousand years old or older. and continues to be performed by modern Ute. The bear symbolizes leadership, strength, and wisdom.
